dataset.bars_5m: scratchpad/radar_design/replay/bars_5m_prepost.csv.gz (Yahoo 5m incl. extended hours; engine uses regular session only)
dataset.universe: radar/data/universe.csv: 542 rows, 518 stocks + 24 ETFs; non-reference ETFs dropped -> 521 symbols
dataset.sessions: 60 sessions 2026-07-02..2026-09-25; the first 20 only seed baselines; 40 replay sessions

notes: Educational analysis, not financial advice. prec@h is a historical continuation share, not a probability of anything.

Parity with the fp_lens reference (same 39 sessions 2026-08-03..09-25, the 332 symbols both datasets share): the reference REC listed 142 entries on those names; radar.engine lists 134, 133 of them identical (symbol, session, entry bar) and 131 of those with the same exit bar (132 before the 2026-10-06 DATA_STALE fix, see below). Of the 9 reference entries not reproduced, 7 are blocked by the sector cap (max 3 per sector and direction, e.g. 2026-09-22 Financials falling) and 2 sit on a threshold edge (the pooled time-of-day profile depends on the universe). On those names: 3.4 entries/day, prec@30 57.5%, flap 3.7%.

The reference's 58.3% prec@30 on 491 names included 81 entries on 159 high-beta mid caps (GME, SNAP, DKNG, ...) that are not in the 542-name S&P 500 + Nasdaq-100 universe; that composition difference, not a logic difference, explains the lower prec@30 and volume here.
Determinism: rebuilding the Engine from its JSON state_dict on every tick reproduces the same REC scorecard; the largest engine state was 37 KB and the largest snapshot 7 KB over the 40 sessions.

Re-run 2026-10-06 after the SPEC 12.2 engine amendments. On recorded bars only the DATA_STALE rule changes the result: it now counts consecutive bars without a fresh print instead of 3-bar windows. REC entries, prec@15/30/60, hold30, dwell and flap rate are unchanged; the one REC exit that was DATA_STALE (EXPE 2026-09-23, down, entered slot 21) came from a single zero-volume Yahoo bar at slot 22 and read 'No fresh 5-minute bars for 3 scans' at slot 24; it now exits on FADE at slot 26. The naive baseline loses its DATA_STALE exits as well (3785 -> 3784 entries). The other amendments (quotes_ok, degraded_volume, provisional bars, stored names and sectors, banner pruning, SPY prior-close check) do not act on a replay of complete Yahoo bars.

Re-run 2026-10-07 after the second DATA_STALE fix (any fresh print now ends a stale run, also on fallback bars, which only never add to it): the scorecard is identical to the 2026-10-06 run apart from runtime, as a replay never feeds fallback bars.
